title: Your Ears Get 0.22 mm Longer Every Year 👂
description:
Why do your ears and nose keep getting longer as you age? Adult ears and noses aren't really growing: collagen and elastin fibers weaken with age and gravity slowly stretches the cartilage and skin, with earlobes sagging the most.

topic: Why do your ears and nose seem to keep growing as you age?
script: Your ears never stop getting longer, but they aren't growing. Your nose droops lower every year too. So what's stretching them? Your bones stopped getting longer years ago. The floppy parts of your ears and nose are cartilage and skin, held up by springy fibers called collagen and elastin. As you get older, your body makes fewer of those fibers. The springs get weaker, and gravity wins. Every single year it pulls them down a tiny bit more. Earlobes stretch the most, because there's no cartilage inside them at all. Just skin and fat. One study of two hundred and six adults found ears get about zero point two two millimeters longer every year after age thirty. That's roughly a whole centimeter by eighty. So nothing's growing. Your face is just slowly sagging. So how much longer will your ears be at a hundred?
key_facts: Adult ears and noses lengthen and droop with age, but not from tissue growth like in childhood (Live Science)
Main cause: less collagen and elastin plus gravity, making earlobes sag and the nose tip droop (Live Science, aging wiki)
Earlobes elongate most because they have no cartilage, only fibrofatty tissue (aging wiki)
Heathcote 1995 BMJ, 206 adults aged 30-93: ear length rises about 0.22 mm per year (aging wiki summary of BMJ study)
0.22 mm x 50 years (30 to 80) is about 11 mm, roughly 1 cm
